« Hood Heroes », épisode 18 – Birdzonthe: “Hood Heroes,” Episode 18 – Birdzonthetrack, youth worker by day, beatmaker by night
Vous connaissez Birdzonthetrack ? Le pro: Do you know Birdzonthetrack? The Montréal producer-composer works with big names in both the local and European music industries.
Birdzontrack, un beatmaker local, au stu: Birdzontrack, a local beatmaker, at Toosik studio in Montréal. (Photo: Julien Forest, La Converse)
J’ai connu Birdzonthetrack au fil des an: I’ve known of Birdzonthetrack over the years because of his work in the music scene. He’s a producer in the local hip-hop industry, but he also works a lot with French artists I listen to.
C’est lorsqu’il m’a confié, au cours d’u: It was when he told me, during a chance encounter, that he had been a youth worker for years that I found it interesting. The dichotomy between his Bruce Wayne side – youth work by day – and his Batman side – music producer by night – paints the portrait of someone devoted to his passion, but also to the well-being of young people and of society.
Il n’a pas été facile de convaincre Bird: It wasn’t easy to convince Birdzonthetrack to be interviewed and filmed for a segment of the “Hood Heroes” series, even though he perfectly embodies the idea of someone from the hood who made it and gives back to the community. It was after spending a lot of time in the world of La Converse – with his participation in the MC Converse project (a new edition coming out in September 2024) – that he finally reversed his decision and accepted our request. He explained that he wanted to share his journey in order to inspire and motivate young people.
Je vous laisse découvrir Birdzonthetrack: I’ll let you discover Birdzonthetrack, producer and beatmaker, but also a youth worker who plays the role of big brother to many young people in need.
Bonne lecture et à bientôt !: Happy reading, and see you soon!
Si vous êtes un amateur de rap local, il: If you’re a fan of local rap, there’s a good chance you’ve already heard the work of Birdzonthetrack, a producer and composer from here. Lendcey, as he’s called by his first name, is well established today: he works with big names in the local industry as well as with artists from the global industry, notably in Europe. While his experience in the music world has allowed him to perform on a more underground scene, it’s his role as a youth worker that has filled his days for the past few years. An intimate conversation with Birdz, who only rarely steps into the spotlight.
« J’ai un parcours assez normal, assure: “I’ve had a pretty normal path,” Lendcey insists. “I went to high school at Joseph-François-Perrault, in the Saint-Michel neighbourhood. That’s where I’m from, originally.” He then continued his studies at CEGEP and university, where he enrolled in psychology and sociology so he could work in the field of intervention.
Pour lui, qui est aujourd’hui dans la vi: For him, now in his twenties, things haven’t always been easy. “There were times when I doubted myself, when I felt imposter syndrome,” he recalls. “Did I belong there? Did I deserve to be where I was? Because of my skin colour or the neighbourhood I grew up in, was I not supposed to be here? I was often confronted with an inner struggle, with those questions. I questioned myself a lot,” he tells us in a moment of sincerity.
Mis face à ses propres inquiétudes, Bird: Faced with his own worries, Birdz is nonetheless certain of one thing: he has always liked finding solutions. “Especially for young people, because I identify with them a lot. The ‘problem youth’ are often kids who come from the neighbourhoods,” he tells us.
Lendcey a grandi entre Saint-Michel et M: Lendcey grew up between Saint-Michel and Montréal-Nord. “I’m not saying I made it, but I managed to get out of it,” he clarifies. He remembers his high school years, when the guidance counsellor told him more than once that he and others like him “weren’t going to go far.” That kind of comment made him doubt himself on many occasions.
« Et puis, je vois le chemin que j’ai pa: “And then, I see the road I’ve travelled in spite of everything. That’s where I think I can be an example for young people,” he says, more positively. Birdzonthetrack strongly believes in the potential young people have and thinks we need to find the right ways to tap into it. “Youth work led me to work on myself, and that’s very important too,” he adds.
Loin de croire que la musique est pour l: Far from believing music is a gift for him, Birdz recounts his first contacts with the art form. “I don’t know if it’s true,” he begins, laughing, “but my mother tells me that when I was two or three years old, I liked to bang on pots and pans and play drums with them.” A few years later, his mother decided to sign him up for piano lessons. He had planned to go on to study at a music conservatory, but changed his mind. “I found classical music too boring,” he recalls. “I wanted to create and learn, I wanted to spread my own wings.”
À l’âge de 17 ans, il commence à s’impli: At 17, he started getting seriously involved in music composition. One of his best friends – Lucky, he wants to specify – pushed him to put himself out there so his work would be seen and heard by as many people as possible. “I remember Lucky logged into my email and sent my tracks to a bunch of rappers in the city. Among them, White-B, from the group 5Sang14, got back to me because he was interested in my work. That’s how, little by little, I started making a place for myself in the music world.”
<strong>« Un gars de Montréal qui essaie: “A guy from Montréal trying to make his own way”
Si son chemin est inspirant, il n’a pas: While his path is inspiring, it hasn’t been without obstacles. “A lot of the difficulties I faced were tied to myself,” he begins. “I always put pressure on myself that, often, wasn’t necessary.” Academically, his first year of university was the hardest. “I was the only Black guy in my cohort, the only one from the hood too. It was hard, but I managed to adapt, slowly.”
La conciliation travail-école a aussi ét: Balancing work and school was also a challenge for Lendcey. “Juggling music, exams, the end of the semester, it was complicated,” he recalls. “I remember times when I’d stay at the studio with artists until the early morning and then go study for my exam the next morning. It was something!”
Mais ce qui a été le plus délicat, ç’a é: But the most delicate part was getting his parents to accept what he was passionate about: beatmaking. “As the son of immigrants, I can say our parents often want us to pursue higher education and hold prestigious positions. So when you tell your parents you want to do beatmaking, they don’t even know what that is, and they have all their stereotypes about the rap world,” he says. Today, it’s a different story: Birdz says his parents are extremely proud of him and support him in his passion.
Le jeune producteur estime qu’il a su jo: The young producer feels he has played the cards life dealt him: “Just because you come from a certain background doesn’t mean you can’t succeed. To keep it simple, I’m a guy from Montréal trying to make his own way.”
<strong>Comprendre les jeunes, c’est aid: Understanding young people means helping young people
Lorsqu’il est question des jeunes et des: When it comes to young people and ways to help them, Birdz joins the conversation with heart. It’s easy to believe that Montréal’s youth are at risk, misunderstood and lost. For the youth worker, we have to set aside what we might think and try to understand the youngest generation.
« Je ne pense pas qu’ils soient perdus,: “I don’t think they’re lost,” he says of the city’s teenagers and young adults. “I think they’re looking for reference points. They’re looking for validation, they’re looking for a family, a sense of belonging, and even self-esteem.”
Si les jeunes sont tant à la recherche d: If young people are so hungry for approval, it’s because they’re trying to fill a gap, according to this lover of rhythm. Faced with this lack of understanding and the fog of complexity surrounding young people, Birdz has no answer to offer, but he puts forward several hypotheses.
« On essaie toujours de trouver des solu: “We always try to find solutions when a young person falls into delinquency, but what we’re trying to fix and heal, we do without asking the young people. Yet they’re the ones most directly affected. The solution has to come from young people, not from us,” he says in one breath. “Our youth need to feel welcomed, valued for who they are. And just because they make mistakes doesn’t mean they’ll necessarily end up better or worse off, or turn out badly,” says Birdzonthetrack. After all, to err is human, he reminds us, and “we tend to forget that.”
Les jeunes sont conscients que le monde: Young people are aware that the world isn’t doing well. “They see that there doesn’t seem to be a way out, and that sometimes, nobody helps them get out. They’ll try to get out on their own. We have to give them advice and wisdom, not judgment. There has to be dialogue between us, and it comes with acceptance, tolerance and respect,” he says thoughtfully.
Toujours dans la lumière crue du studio: Still in the harsh light of the recording studio, Birdz tells anecdotes from his journey and the experiences that led him to become the man he is today. And for him, it all comes down to choices. “When I was younger, I tried to be careful about my actions. Before making a choice, small or big, I always looked at three things. First, will I be able to stand by my choice? Second, will my actions have an impact on my loved ones or my family? Finally, in a few years, will I tell myself I made the right choice?”
Ces réflexions semblent rapides et anodi: These reflections may seem quick and harmless, but Birdz insists that it’s important to be mindful of your actions, whether toward yourself or toward others. He’s also aware of reality and knows it’s possible, and normal, to make mistakes and bad choices. “If you get it wrong in life, it’s okay. What matters is that you get back up and keep going,” he says, inspiringly. “Know that you’ll always have help,” the beatmaker finally concludes. Here, he’s speaking to young people, especially those who want to get into music.
Pour lui, la musique est venue le sauver: For him, music came to save him. So he knows how many people it can keep busy and inspire. “There are plenty of organizations that help young people who are starting out, whether it’s <l1>SOCAN</l1> or <l2>SODEC</l2>, to name just those two.”
Autodidacte, Birdz encourage les autres: Self-taught, Birdz encourages others not to be afraid to take the leap, even if they think they don’t have the level or the courage.
La soirée se termine doucement, mais sûr: The evening comes to a slow but steady close. Birdzonthetrack, in his element, gets back to working on his music. Watching the young man in front of his computer using his audio editing software, it feels like watching a fish in water. While Birdz doesn’t much like putting himself out there in the media, La Converse still stepped into his world for the length of one meeting. “I’m someone who likes to protect my privacy, but I always like to let my music speak for me,” he concludes.
